questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The subjects provided at the university, the language and opportunity to explore a completely different nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: University of Melbourne were really good at providing good orientation about choosing/changing subjects, the online communication platform as so forth, to have a nice and easy start at the university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The orientation week is filled with information on different society and sports clubs and general information on how to study at UniMelb.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It depends on how much money you're willing to spend. I found my housing quite randomly within the first days I arrived. In general, it is easy to find accommodation upon arrival, as you quickly start talking to a lot of people. My best advice is not to stress about finding accommodation, as you will get a place to live eventually. Either through different Facebook groups or through people you meet.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is much cheaper living off campus and the public transportation in Melbourne is so easy. Almost all the trams leads to UniMelb.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for subjects online, which is quite easy but will take some time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can easily contact the university if you have any questions. They are really nice and quick to answer.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all the subjects I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: University of Melbourne offers a lot of "different" subjects, such as meditation, wine tasting etc. So if you're allowed (from the home university) to take those kind of subjects, I would really recommend. I regret not taking those, as other people I met seemed to really connect with other students through those courses. Otherwise, take a good amount of time to look through the courses. There are plenty and it will be hard to choose. However, you are allowed to change the subjects within the first couple of weeks you start.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the overall academic level were similar to Copenhagen university. However, the whole learning system is a bit different with many assignments during the semester that will all be a part of the overall score for the course and thus, the final grade. Therefore, I think it is easier to pass the courses compared to Copenhagen uni.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Australia the university courses are evaluated during the whole semester. Therefore, the study load is bigger than Copenhagen uni based on assignments and quizzes. You might also have more than one exam in a particular course. On the other hand, the presssure from the final exams are less intensive, as you will already have passed part of the courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Medical Microbiology: Parasitology. Medical Microbiology: virology. Advanced Molecular Biology Techniques. Developmental Neurobiology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Developmental Neurobiology and Medical Microbiology: Parasitology were both courses that I really enjoyed following. The teaching and feedback is really good as well as the topics covered.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Flight tickets were more expensive than expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing costs in Melbnourne depends on where you're willing to stay and how long you're willing to wait for accommodation but in general a bit more expensive than Copenhagen. Otherwise, the living costs are comparable to Copenhagen (except beers, which are really expensive ;))

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I used the sports facilities provided by the university a lot, which was really good.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: University of Melbourne has everything! All kinds of sports and social clubs!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do engage in some of the social or sports clubs. You will meet other nice people, and there is for sure one club that will fit you.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go around Melbourne and explore the Victoria state. There is so much beautiful and incredible nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Melbourne is not that different from Copenhagen in that sense, so you will easily adjust to that.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open and talk to the fellow student in your classes. Otherwise, engage in some sport or social club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Melbourne is a super cool city with a lot of social and artistic culture. There is many really good restaurants and bars and you can almost always find live music.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't worry about accommodation if you haven't figured it out from home, you will find it when you arrive.
Go explore the state Victoria, it is so amazing. 
Do attend the orientation week as you will easily find some people to talk to, which is nice when you don't know anyone in the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Buy a bike. It is cheap in Melbourne and you will be able to easily get around.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting really good people to have in the daily Melbourne life. Traveling around Melbourne during weekends to see the wild nature of Australia.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being completely on your own at the beginning of the stay, which is something different that you need to figure out how to cope with.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
